pr_title: Bump Explicit-layout value types with no fields to at minimum 1 byte size.
pr_body:
Fixes #63664

cc: @jeffschwMSFT this PR should fix the WPF AppCompat issues.

2). Windows10 RS5 x64+dotnet-sdk-7.0.100-alpha.1.21568.2: Pass

**App Source and App Checking at:** https://devdiv.visualstudio.com/DevDiv/_workitems/edit/1460206

**Findings:**
1)  Compare the PresentationCore.dll version from dotnet-sdk-7.0.100-alpha.1.22057.7 and dotnet-sdk-7.0.100-alpha.1.21568.2, we found they have different versions. In dotnet-sdk-7.0.100-alpha.1.22057.7, it is 7.0.22.5501, and in dotnet-sdk-7.0.100-alpha.1.21568.2, it is 7.0.21.56606.
2) Since the error is unable to load 'System.Windows.Media.MILCMD_POP' type from PresentationCore.dll, we use ILSpy to reflect the PresentationCore.dll, and found 'System.Windows.Media.MILCMD_POP' type exists in dotnet-sdk-7.0.100-alpha.1.22057.7 and the access modifier is internal, no difference with dotnet-sdk-7.0.100-alpha.1.21568.2.
3) We tried retarget the app from .netcore3.0 to .net 7.0, the same exception when finding 'System.Windows.Media.MILCMD_POP' type.

comments:
Hey @Junjun-zhao,
This is unrelated to WPF. Here is a simple repro that does not use WPF and reproduces this issue:
```
Assembly.GetEntryAssembly().GetType("MILCMD_POP");

[StructLayout(LayoutKind.Explicit)]
internal struct MILCMD_POP
{
}
```

Tested with 7.0.0-alpha.1.22055.1.

I recommend opening an issue in [dotnet/runtime](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime).

I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. If you have write-permissions please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).
@mangod9 and @trylek can you take a look at this?
Dont believe there have been specific changes related to `LayoutKind.Explicit`, since this is reproing via reflection perhaps @agocke @AaronRobinsonMSFT are aware of some changes here?
/cc @jkoritzinsky who worked on the runtime type layout cleanup, I believe that did involve subtle changes to explicit & sequential types
Verify with dotnet-sdk-7.0.100-preview.1.22076.2, it has been fixed.

review_comments: Just for my education - does the same logic hold for zero-sized classes with explicit layout i.o.w. should we be also testing correct behavior in the presence of inheritance?
I believe zero-sized classes are already bumped up to at least 1-byte elsewhere, but to make sure I've added some more test cases to make sure.
We don't need to specifically validate inheritance as it will end up down the same code path as the non-inheritance case.
